name: Full-service hotel
summary: Upscale / upper-upscale full-service hotel (~200–500 keys, mid/high-rise concrete or steel) with restaurant and bar, ballroom and meeting space, and full back-of-house. Cost per key is driven by public-space ratio (meeting/F&B SF per key), structure and urban location; structured parking can add materially. Good national data from four HVS cost-survey editions, plus RLB 2026 metro $/SF and RSMeans national models.

typicalSize.method: HCEG prototypes: upscale 304 rooms (9 stories), upper upscale 192 rooms + 25 suites (e20). Convention/headquarters hotels exceed 500 keys; mid 300.

sfPerPrimaryUnit.method: Net guestroom 389–472 SF (HCEG upscale / upper upscale, e21) + bath ~70 SF ≈ 460–540 SF; guestroom floors ~0.70 efficient → ~650–770 GSF/key; plus F&B, ballroom/meeting (HCEG upscale prototype: 3,000 SF restaurant, 8,550 SF ballroom, 11,900 SF meeting for 304 rooms ≈ 77 SF/key) with pre-function, kitchens and BOH roughly doubling that → ~150–350 SF/key. Total ~800–1,300; mid 1,000.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Suburban mid-rise (8–10 stories, surface + partial deck) ~60–100 keys/acre; urban high-rise on 1–2 acres 200–400+. Mid 120 is a judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: HCEG upscale prototype assumes 1.6 spaces/room to accommodate meeting attendance (e22); downtown hotels often 0.3–0.7 with valet/shared garages. Structured where urban; surface in suburban sites.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS full-service building & site improvements per key (median / average): 2025 data $305,266 / $374,355 (e1); 2024 data $275,414 / $317,731 (e2); 2023 data $261,058 / $315,095 (e3); 2021–22 data $250,762 / $340,996 (e4). x0.91 removes permits, engineering and hard contingency (HVS includes them): 2025 median → $278k, average → $341k. Mid $290k ≈ 0.91 x midpoint of the 2025-data median and the 2024-data average. HVS includes parking garages where built, so the mid is kept below the averages (our baseline excludes structured parking). Cross-checks: RSMeans 15-story national $261.76/SF (2025, incl. ~6% A/E, building only, e7) x 1,000 SF ≈ $247k ex-A/E before sitework; RLB 2026 large-metro 3-star $343–$475/SF and 5-star $483–$735/SF (e5, e6) x 1,000 SF ≈ $400k–$600k (metro). Low $210k ≈ 0.91 x the 2021–2023-data medians less a secondary-market discount; high $420k ≈ RLB 3-star metro midpoint x 1,000 SF ≈ 0.91 x 2025 average + urban premium.

perSF.method: Mid = $290k ÷ 1,000 SF. RSMeans national 15-story hotel $261.76/SF in 2025 (e7) — ~$247 excluding the 6% A/E fee in RSMeans model totals (e8), building only; RSMeans 4–7 story $181–$197/SF in 2019 dollars (e9). RLB 2026 metro 3-star median midpoint $406, 5-star $613 (e5, e6). Low ≈ RSMeans national less A/E; high ≈ RLB metro 3-star median-high.

scope.notes: Contractor price incl. GC and OH&P, on-site work (drives, porte-cochère, landscaping, utilities); ballroom/meeting/F&B space built out (fixed finishes). Excludes land, structured parking (add from the parking block), FF&E incl. kitchen equipment, OS&E, pre-opening, permits, contingency, soft costs, off-sites, impact/tap fees and financing.

qualityTiers.method: Economy ≈ low/mid (0.72, rounded up to 0.8 for full-service minimum program); premium ≈ high/mid (1.45) trimmed to 1.35; luxury from HVS luxury vs. full-service median building cost: 2025 data $916,919 / $305,266 = 3.0 (e18), 2024 data $620,471 / $275,414 = 2.25 (e19); 2.0 used because luxury resorts are a separate type.

systemSplit.method: No public elemental breakdown found. Derived for a concrete/steel mid-to-high-rise: structure (03/05) ~16%; curtain wall/storefront and doors (08) 7%; finishes (09) 12% with heavier public-space finishes; central plant HVAC (23) and plumbing (22) 8% each; multiple traction elevators/service cars (14) 4%; built-in kitchen/laundry rough-ins and fixed equipment (11) 3%; sitework (31–33) ~7%. Verify against a GMP schedule of values.

lineItems.name: Pre-opening, OS&E and working capital

cost.method: HVS full-service pre-opening & working capital per key: 2025 data $11,842 median / $14,075 avg (e14); 2024 data $8,796 / $14,594 (e15). Mid ≈ 2025 median; range spans the medians/averages.

lineItems.notes: Owner cost: pre-opening staffing/training/marketing, OS&E (linen, china/glass/silver, uniforms, operating supplies), operating reserves, technical services fees.

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS full-service FF&E per key: 2025 data $36,752 median / $43,928 avg (e10); 2024 data $34,464 / $39,907 (e11). Mid ≈ 2025 median rounded up; includes commercial kitchen and laundry equipment, public-space and meeting furniture, technology.

pctOfHard.method: HVS soft ÷ building & site improvements (medians): 2025 data 68,842/305,266 = 22.6% (e12); 2024 data 56,081/275,414 = 20.4% (e13). HVS soft costs include construction financing (excluded here) while HVS building costs include permits/engineering (soft here); net mid 20%. Excludes developer fee (HVS 2025-data median $15,857/key).

softCosts.notes: Includes A/E, interior design, kitchen/laundry/AV/IT consultants, brand technical-services and franchise application fees (or management-company technical services for managed hotels — HVS lists the franchise application fee in soft costs; amount is brand-specific), legal, insurance, permits, testing.

design.method: More custom programs (F&B concepts, meeting space) than prototype hotels → higher design contingency at concept stage.

hard.method: Typical new-construction hard-cost contingency; HVS budgets carry hard contingency within building costs (removed by the x0.91 factor).

perPrimaryUnit.method: HVS all-in total less land: 2025 data $467,244 − $30,300 ≈ $437k median, $595,252 − $69,655 ≈ $526k average (e16); 2024 data ≈ $380k median (e17). Totals include FF&E, pre-opening, financing and developer fee. Range widened for secondary markets (low) and urban/convention hotels with structured parking (high).

openQuestions: A public convention-center hotel GMP (city-owned hotel bonds) would give a sourced CSI split and parking carve-out.
Structured parking per space should come from the shared parking building block when available.
HVS medians mix urban and suburban projects; a metro-specific cut would sharpen the low/high.
